previous_revision: REJECT of efe70bc94999 (hang when a rotated latch had 'Bcc exit; j header' and L->getExitBlock() was null; note misdescribed the bump rule). Both points are addressed.
warnings_checked: scripts/policy_check.py --range 6e4c7f2a471f..d01e531f008b --stack-base llvmorg-20.1.8: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN. Single commit, passes-cluster fixup subject, Change-Note trailer, only the fork file PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp touched, no test or upstream file edited.

(1) removeUncountableLoops (PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp ~:262-285) is a justified rule-9 bail-out: it deletes only the LOOPsetup, and only when L->getLoopLatch() is null (several back edges, i.e. a tail-duplicated latch whose iterations the hardware would not count) or the setup's latch has no single out-of-loop successor (hardware has one fall-out point). The software loop is intact at that point: PULPHardwareLoops never erases the loop branch (it only calls removeIfDead on IV/compare defs, which the branch keeps alive; PULPHardwareLoops.cpp:1376-1377), and the latch branch/bump removal happens later in fixupLoopLatch. The count copy becomes a dead value. Loops with one back edge and one latch exit are not affected. Fuzz: 15 of 1236 compiling builds lose a hardware loop to it (7 of those were miscompiled by int-20), all correct.

(2) fixupLoopLatch now uses getLatchExit(L, LastMBB) instead of L->getExitBlock(): for 'Bcc exit; j header' the Bcc target equals the latch exit, so both terminators are erased and 'j exit' inserted in the same round. For a single-exit-edge loop it is the same block as before. Reviewer hang seeds 22 (O2/O3/Os) and 13 (O2; Os now compiles and is correct; O3 is an F003 crash in both builds) run correctly.

(3) fixupLoopLayout additionally moves a unique latch that sits inside the Header..Bottom run but is followed by other loop blocks; guarded by LastMBB != Bottom, != Header and L->getLoopLatch()==LastMBB; same splice + keepFallthrough repair (ARMBlockPlacement::moveBasicBlock pattern). All moved/remaining range blocks are loop blocks; a contiguous sub-loop cannot be split. Seed 270 -O2 (int-20 wrong) is now correct. Confirmed by hand on seed 1362 -O2 ('for(..){ if(c) continue; acc+=..; }'): int-20 ends the hardware loop on the then-path and skips the i++ latch (wrong result on GVSoC); F005 ends the range at the latch followed by 'j exit'.

(4) Empty latch NOP: notes/20/F005-reduced-emptylatch.ll crashes int-20 llc -O3 with !isKnownSentinel and compiles with F005 to 'lp.setup; p.lw zero,4(a0!); nop(end)', same technique as the existing inline-asm NOP workaround.

(5) Counter-increment rule: now 'CandMBB == LastMBB ? non-terminators <= 1 : size() <= 2', i.e. unchanged for non-latch blocks and identical to size()<=2 for a single-branch latch; the note now describes this correctly.
getLayoutBottom / getDebugLoc reorder unchanged from revision 1 (correct).
